approved: Marriage Amendment (Celebrant Administration and Fees) Bill 2013

Introduced the Marriage Amendment (Celebrant Administration and Fees) Bill implementing a 2011 budget decision to introduce cost recovery for the Marriage Celebrants Program, established in 1973, noting 71 per cent of marriages in 2011 were conducted by a civil celebrant, and detailed new fees from 1 July 2013 of $600 for registration, $240 annually and $30 for exemption applications.

Moved that the Marriage Amendment (Celebrant Administration and Fees) Bill 2013, Marriage (Celebrant Registration Charge) Bill 2013 and Therapeutic Goods Amendment (2013 Measures No. 1) Bill 2013 be referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration.

Detailed the three categories of marriage celebrants under the bills, including approximately 24,500 ministers of religion, 730 state officers and 10,500 Commonwealth registered celebrants, noted the new fee would be capped at $600 in 2013-14, and said celebrant numbers grew from 3,632 in 2003 to 10,467 in 2012.

Spoke on the Marriage Celebrant bills, quoting a submission from Marriage Celebrants Australia noting 70 per cent of Australians choose a civil ceremony while religious celebrants, used by the other 30 per cent, avoid the new fee, and said the average celebrant performs seven weddings a year for a gross income of about $3,500.
